assets.prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Create a sophisticated Czech scientific illustration for adult readers of Klimatologie.eu, 1536x1024 landscape. Warm ivory background, dark petrol text, restrained blue ocean, terracotta warm water. Title "Jak se teplý výkyv zesiluje". A scientifically clear two-panel east-west vertical section along equatorial Pacific. Left edge of each panel WEST Indonesia, right edge EAST South America. Top panel heading "Běžné podmínky": trade winds arrows point RIGHT TO LEFT, label "Pasáty ženou vodu na západ". Warm upper layer thick in west, thin in east. A clearly labelled thermocline line slopes UP toward east. Cold blue below. Modest upwelling arrow in east up into surface label "Výstup chladnější vody". Rain clouds in west and rising moist air. Bottom panel heading "Rozvoj El Niño": weakened leftward trade winds, label "Slabší pasáty". Warm surface water extends east, thermocline flatter with deeper east end than above. Label at east "Voda přicházející k povrchu je teplejší". Convective rain clouds move from west toward central Pacific. Label "Déšť a výstup vzduchu se posouvají na východ". Make large clean margins and beautiful ocean depth rendering, physical mechanism rather than decorative icons. On right beside panels, a compact explanatory feedback loop in 3 boxes and directional arrows: "Teplejší povrch na východě" → "Změna deště a proudění vzduchu" → "Další oslabení pasátů" → back to first. Loop label "Zesilující zpětná vazba". Bottom footer: "Sledujeme společně teplotu vody, hloubku termokliny a vítr." and small "Kvalitativní schéma, nikoli naměřený profil". Define with small label "Termoklina: vrstva rychlého poklesu teploty s hloubkou". Avoid fake numerical graphs, no sun icon, no arbitrary numerical values, no dramatic ocean sea-level slopes. All labels Czech with correct accents and legible. Ocean panels should dominate, feedback loop takes right quarter. No extra labels, no tiny bibliography.

Use case: scientific-educational. Create a polished adult Czech explanatory graphic for Klimatologie.eu, 1536x1024 landscape, matching ivory, dark petrol, muted ocean blue and terracotta warm-water style. Title "Oceán si uchovává předchozí vývoj". Four equal cards arranged clockwise 1 upper-left, 2 upper-right, 3 lower-right, 4 lower-left. Thin arrows between cards clearly give order 1→2→3→4→1. Each card contains an oblique 3D ocean slab of the central/eastern equatorial Pacific, with transparent sides showing a warm orange upper layer above blue cold water. Label the equatorial band in each slab "Rovníkové pásmo". No continents or exact coastlines needed. This is a basin-average volume illustration, NOT east-west tilt and NOT different entire-ocean heat content. Card1 heading "1. Před teplou fází" and label "Větší zásoba teplé vody pod hladinou": upper warm layer relatively thick, surface neutral teal to show surface need not be warm yet. Card2 heading "2. Během El Niño": top surface warm terracotta. Blue/teal arrows in the horizontal ocean plane carry warm water OUT of the equatorial band toward BOTH north and south, labelled "Teplá voda postupně odtéká od rovníku". Warm layer visibly thinning, caption "Zásoba ubývá, povrch je ještě teplý". Card3 heading "3. Přechod k chladné fázi": thin warm layer and cold blue water close beneath surface, upward arrow from cold water labelled "Chladnější voda se snáze dostává k povrchu". Card4 heading "4. Během La Niña": blue cool surface and growing warm subsurface layer, horizontal arrows flow INTO the equatorial band from both sides, label "Zásoba teplé vody se obnovuje". Make arrows unambiguous transport of WATER in horizontal plane, NOT ocean-atmosphere heat loss. Bottom clear key: "Oranžová vrstva: voda nad hranicí 20 °C. Modrá: chladnější voda." Another footer "Sledujeme změnu zásoby pod hladinou a její předstih před povrchovou teplotou." Small final "Idealizovaná posloupnost. Události nemají pevný kalendář." Elegant scientific illustration, informative realistic cutaways, generous legible typography, no cartoons, no batteries, no sun, no invented plotted data, no quantitative arrows, no implied every El Niño is followed directly by La Niña. Labels exactly Czech.
assets.revision: Edit the provided scientific graphic, preserve title, four numbered cards and the overall design and wording. Correct two scientific ambiguities precisely. 1. All four ocean slabs must have an ORANGE top surface continuously connected to the orange upper layer: even La Niña surface water here stays warmer than 20 °C. Do NOT draw blue/cyan surface lying on top of warm orange water. Keep colder blue ONLY below the orange layer. Vary the orange layer thickness: card1 thick, card2 intermediate thinning, card3 thin, card4 thicker than card3 as it rebuilds. Add small neutral text chips above slab in card1 "Povrch: blízko obvyklé teploty", card2 "Povrch: teplejší než obvykle", card3 "Povrch: chladnější než obvykle", card4 "Povrch: chladnější než obvykle". Do not use absolute cold blue surface for relative cool phases. 2. In card4, arrows must enter the dashed equatorial band from the NORTH and SOUTH sides, meaning from back and front sides of the slab in this oblique perspective. They must be the geometric reverse of outward arrows shown in card2, not flow left-to-right along the equator. Draw a single inward arrow from back toward middle and a single inward arrow from front toward middle. Label slab far side "Sever" and front side "Jih" in cards2 and4 to clarify. Keep card2 outward arrows pointing from equatorial band toward north/back and south/front. Everything else keep. No invented data. Make all text fit cleanly.
